title: Edge GPU reclaim + network reminders
content:
Morning scratchpad - edge GPU reclaim + network quirks

Context: quick personal checklist for reclaiming idle GPUs on edge clusters (eu-west/edge-1 and us-west/edge-2). Also capture networking hairpin/NAT oddities we hit during last maintenance. Not a runbook — notes to flesh out later and maybe fold into the runbook PR (see linked PR).

Top priorities (today)
- [ ] Reclaim idle GPUs in edge-1 (threshold: idle > 30m, mem < 4GB) - start with node pool 'edge-gpu-a'
- [ ] Verify BGP sessions with colo for edge-2 before any node drains (if BGP flaps, rollback drain)
- [ ] Patch kube-proxy on 3 nodes with hairpin fix (iptables ambiguous chains)
- [ ] Follow up on INF-4872: automated eviction job failing intermittently (see logs)

Quick checklist / Commands
- Find idle CUDA processes: ps aux | grep -E "(python|tensorflow|torch)" | grep -v kubelet
- Check GPU utilization: kubectl -n infra exec -it <node-debug-pod> -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv
- Drain node gracefully: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m
- Force delete orphaned pods if stuck: kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force
- Trigger reclaim job (local): ./scripts/edge-reclaim --cluster edge-1 --dry-run && ./scripts/edge-reclaim --cluster edge-1
- Quick iptables check for hairpin: sudo iptables -t nat -L -v --line-numbers | grep DNAT || echo "no DNAT rules"

Notes on hairpin/NAT behavior (recurring)
- Observed: hairpin NAT drops after kube-proxy upgrade; client->service->pod traffic returns RST randomly. Suspect conflicting nat PREROUTING rules when kube-proxy iptables mode coexists with custom DNAT rules created by our NAT gateway.
- Temporary mitigation: recreate kube-proxy configmap with 'hairpinMode: Promiscuous' and restart kube-proxy on the three affected nodes. Need to validate latency impact.
- Long term: upstream ticket? Capture packet traces if happens again (tcpdump -i any port 5000, filter by src/dst).

Eviction/automation quirks
- Eviction job (edge-evictor) sometimes picks up pods that are already in Terminating state which leads to double-delete and API errors. Add a pre-check for .status.phase != Terminating in the controller loop.
- Logged a flaky race at controller loops in INF-4872; Miguel to reproduce with stronger logging (we agreed on extra context: nodeName, pod UID, lastTransitionTime).

Metrics & thresholds to watch (for today)
- GPU reclaim: idle windows > 30m and mem < 4GB => safe to evict (except for pods with runtimeClass 'pinned-gpu')
- Node readiness flaps: >3 reboots in 24h -> mark for manual inspection
- BGP flaps: >2 neigh resets in 10m -> abort drains & notify network

Customer impact notes
- Dedicated customers on edge-2 run latency-sensitive services; avoid simultaneous drains on both AZs during business hours (08:00-18:00 PT). If forced, set canary drain for 5 min and watch per-route SLOs.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should reclaim job consider pod annotation 'redwood/keep-on-idle=true' (product asked for this, need product input)
- Add alert for 'edge-evictor' restarts >2 in 1h
- Validate hairpin fix on staging with a BGP peer configured (create lightweight peer using exa-peer VM)

Micro-tasks (for the shift)
- 09:10: kick off dry-run for edge-1 reclaim (tag: @miguel on slack if weird pods)
- 09:40: check BGP session status (birdcl / show ip bgp) and post summary to #infra-ops
- 10:15: roll kube-proxy config on affected nodes (one-at-a-time)
- 11:00: run tcpdump if any hairpin failures observed; save pcap to /tmp/edge-hairpin-<ts>.pcap
- 14:00: review INF-4872 logs + open follow-up ticket for eviction pre-check

Reminders to self
- write short blurb for product about adding annotation toggle for keep-on-idle
- update runbook with the iptables hairpin example + tcpdump commands

Scratch notes (raw)
- If drain times out: kubectl uncordon and try smaller pod-eviction-timeout on next attempt
- nvidia-driver hot-reload: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced; if XID errors keep appearing, escalate to driver team
- There was a weird NAT rule created by third-party load-balancer (lb-xyz) on edge-2; contact network owner if seen again

Slack refs
- #gpu-ops (pinned msg about reclaim script), #infra-ops (BGP flaps), #oncall (escalation)

End of scratchpad for today. Save and trim into runbook PR later.
plain_text_preview: Morning checklist for reclaiming idle GPUs on edge clusters and networking hairpin notes. Includes commands, thresholds, micro-tasks, and open questions.
